image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Retain the native grasp; shift the visible plug slightly left toward the socket while lowering cautiously. Depth and rotational alignment remain uncertain.
The plug remains held and nearly centered over the visible slit. Close the remaining vertical gap in small increments while maintaining orientation and grip.
The plug tip is immediately above the slot and laterally centered. Lower another 2 mm cautiously to reach the socket mouth; keep the grasp closed.
The tip now meets the socket opening. Begin shallow insertion with small vertical increments; watch for blocked motion or plug displacement.
At the mouth, reduce the small tool tilt and yaw toward a vertical insertion orientation. Compensate hand translation to approximately keep the plug tip centered, without pushing deeper.
Finish the small vertical-orientation correction with tip-position compensation and advance only 1.25 mm into the socket; maintain the grasp.
The connector stays centered at the socket mouth. Continue a slow 2 mm seating advance, watching the visible plug and finger clearance rather than relying on tracking accuracy.
Apply a final shallow seating increment while preserving alignment. The plug outline is stationary at the mouth, so avoid a large push and inspect for slipping or obstruction.
Hold the aligned seating pose to let contact settle. The plug is flush with the socket region, but insertion depth is occluded; avoid additional downward travel for now.
Make a sub-millimeter final seating advance, holding the connector centered and vertical; stop short of further pushing if the outline remains unchanged.
Hold the final seating pose to observe settling. The connector remains at the slot and the hand is near the block, so avoid pushing farther without clearer evidence.
The plug silhouette has not visibly shortened during seating. Gently withdraw 5 mm with the grip maintained to check retention and expose the socket for a small alignment correction.
The plug stayed at the socket during the small withdrawal. Relax the fingers and lift them clear to inspect whether the connector is stably seated, rather than pushing the hand farther down.
The released connector stands upright at the slot with its base hidden in the opening. Lift the open hand slightly farther clear and monitor stability without disturbing it.
Keep the open hand clear. The connector remains upright at the socket after release; observe stability without further contact.
Maintain clearance and observe the released connector at the socket; no visible shift or tilt calls for further contact.
Hold clear with the fingers open while the connector remains stationary in the slot region.
The released plug is stable, but its exposed length suggests it may only be resting at the mouth. Approach with open fingers to regrasp and check alignment rather than assume completion.
Place the pads alongside the upper connector and restore the narrow grasp. Do not press down against the socket during closure.
Use a smaller opening target, then raise only 4.5 mm to check whether the plug follows and to reveal the slot for alignment. Judge retention from the image.
The smaller opening retained the connector during the lift. Re-approach the aligned slit with a very small away-from-camera correction and a slow 3 mm descent.
The plug is centered at the mouth again. Advance 1.5 mm with the narrower grasp while watching for visible seating or sideways motion.
Try a sub-millimeter left and depth correction at the mouth with only 1 mm of downward travel. The insertion depth remains visually uncertain.
Continue a slow 1 mm insertion advance with the corrected lateral alignment; retain the connector and monitor its outline at the socket.
The connector base is flush at the opening and further hand motion has not changed its outline. Release gently and withdraw vertically to avoid disturbing the seated position.
Move the open hand clear of the connector. Its base remains flush with the fixed socket and upright after release; preserve that position and observe.
Hold the open hand clear and monitor the connector, which remains upright and stationary at the socket after release.
Allow the released connector to settle in the socket while keeping the hand clear; avoid disturbing the stable alignment.
The released connector has tipped onto the block, so it was not securely inserted. Approach its lying body with open fingers to recover the grasp before reorienting.
Lower the pads a few millimeters alongside the horizontal connector, keeping the fingertips near the block top, then close to recover it.
Lift the recovered horizontal connector while keeping the fingers closed. Confirm it follows before rotating it upright.
The connector follows the closed fingers. Raise it clear of the block before correcting its horizontal orientation; the tip direction is still uncertain.
Begin rotating the horizontal connector toward tip-down while lifting it. Compensate the hand motion around the grasped body and watch whether the plug follows.
Continue the gradual tip-down rotation with the grasp closed and the connector well above the block. Maintain an approximately fixed grasp center while adding clearance.
Pause rotation to check retention: the small visible connector appears below the pads, so confirm whether it is actually held before continuing.
The connector fell onto the block; the earlier grasp did not survive rotation. Return toward a vertical open-hand approach to recover it with better pad overlap.
Approach the lying housing farther from its exposed metal end and shift right to its observed center. Straighten the hand while remaining open above the block.
Lower to the horizontal housing with better pad overlap and begin closing slowly. Keep the hand stationary before lifting so the fingers can settle around the body.
Finish closing and allow contact to settle, then lift just 2 mm as a retention test before any rotation.
Lift a further 5 mm without rotating to see whether the horizontal housing stays between the pads; retention is still uncertain.
The housing is tipping at the pad ends rather than securely retained. Reposition slightly along its body and lower for greater contact overlap before a much slower lift.
Let the fingers settle around the housing, then test retention with only a 0.6 mm lift. The connector has rotated during closure, so avoid a fast pull.
Test the revised grasp with a slow 3 mm vertical lift, keeping orientation unchanged and checking the housing against the pad edges.
The housing followed the last small lift. Raise it another 7.5 mm without rotation to clear the block and inspect its current tilt before aligning the tip.
The connector followed the lift. Raise its grasp center while making a small tip-down rotation, compensating hand translation; check that the housing rotates with the pads rather than slipping.
Continue the slow pitch correction with extra clearance at the grasp center. The connector still moves with the fingers; inspect its exposed end before approaching the slot.
Keep turning the retained connector toward tip-down with gradual, grasp-centered motion. Raise the connector center slightly to preserve clearance while its tip orientation becomes clearer.
Continue a small, controlled pitch rotation while keeping the connector well above the socket. Its exposed end is still partly occluded, so retain the grasp and reassess before descending.
Continue toward a downward-pointing plug with smaller pitch increments. Move the grasp center away from the camera and slightly upward to maintain clearance and avoid extending the arm too far.
The hand occludes the connector. Turn the grasp slightly sideways about its approximate center, without descending, to reveal the held plug and verify retention before insertion.
Continue the sideways inspection turn while keeping the grasp center above the block. The plug remains occluded, so do not descend or assume retention.
The side view reveals a dark connector near the pads. Make another small grasp-centered pitch correction toward tip-down, keeping the connector above the socket and checking its visible end.
Turn farther sideways around the held connector to expose its tip. Maintain height and the closed grasp; orientation and retention need visual confirmation before another approach.

The connector is still largely hidden. Reduce the pitch while maintaining the sideways view and approximate grasp center, so its exposed end can be inspected instead of continuing an unverified rotation.
Return gradually toward an upright, front-visible grasp while keeping the connector center above the block. Do not descend while its actual orientation remains occluded.
Complete the return to a near-vertical hand while holding the grasp center clear of the socket. This should expose whether the connector is upright or still sideways between the pads.
The connector is visible between the pads again. Remove the remaining yaw and move partway toward the socket, staying well above it to inspect the exposed tip.
Bring the visible connector over the slit and lower while retaining about a centimeter of clearance. Its exposed end is short, so reassess before contact rather than drive the fingers into the block.
Lower the retained connector another 8 mm toward the centered slit, leaving a small visible gap. Keep orientation fixed and inspect the short exposed tip before touching the block.
The exposed connector is much narrower than the socket, suggesting a yaw mismatch after recovery. Lift clear and begin turning about vertical to bring its broad face into alignment.
